page: UpCloud GPU-48xCPU-960GB-4xH100 is a GPU-accelerated server instance built on the KVM hypervisor. The hardware configuration features an x86_64 architecture powered by 48 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8462Y+ processor operating at 2.0 GHz. This processor is paired with 960.0 GB of system memory, yielding 20.0 GB of RAM per core. The server integrates four NVIDIA Hopper H100 GPUs, providing a total of 320 GB of VRAM. Notably, the CPU allocation is shared, and the instance includes no local storage, requiring external storage solutions.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong multi-core and memory capabilities. The instance achieved a top-tier rating in Passmark CPU score (85,426.66) and Passmark CPU extended instructions (117,918.35). Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reached a top-tier speed of 615.79 GB/sec, while single-core stress-ng performance remained average at 2,196.39. Memory bandwidth tests showed top-tier performance for small-block cached reads at 7,649.82 GB/sec, and strong performance for large-block uncached reads at 316.04 GB/sec. For language model workloads, the system processed prompts at 10,308.98 tokens/sec and generated text at 377.14 tokens/sec using a small 135M model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers high resource density by combining a massive 960.0 GB memory footprint with four enterprise-grade H100 GPUs, though the shared CPU allocation represents a potential tradeoff for workloads requiring sustained, dedicated CPU performance. The absence of local storage means storage costs are externalized. This hardware profile is suited for GPU-accelerated workloads such as large language model inference, deep learning training, data science jobs, and memory-intensive database operations.
